payload.rebuttal: fixed: Confirmed the finding by reading package.py (forbidden, read-only): apply_patch always applies the exported patch onto a fresh checkout of the *current* default branch, so a stacked task's combined patch (parent's diff plus the child's own, since export_patch still diffs from spec.base_sha while the checkout starts at stacked_on) is exactly what's needed while the parent's own PR is still open, but becomes unsafe — a false 'conflicts with {default}', or a duplicated landing if both PRs merge — the moment the parent merges separately. The root fix (opening the child's PR against the parent's branch, or refusing to package until the parent is MERGED) lives entirely in saffron/phases/package.py, which is forbidden to this spec. Within touches, I changed cli.py's _run_cell to skip package() entirely for a stacked, green run (outcome.state == READY_FOR_REVIEW and stacked_on is not None): the task still lands READY_FOR_REVIEW in the ledger, but no patch is pushed and no PR opened — instead a printed note tells the operator to package it by hand once the parent has merged. session.py's export_patch docstring now explains why it deliberately keeps diffing from base_sha (apply_patch needs the combined content while the parent's PR is open; diffing from stacked_on instead would make the local patch.diff honest but break the common case where the parent hasn't merged yet). docs/BACKLOG.md item 30 records the gap and what actually closing it requires in package.py, assigning it to the merge train (§6.1). A new test, test_a_stacked_green_run_is_not_packaged, drives cli.main with a stacked outcome and a package() that raises if called, proving the skip — commit 6474545, docs in a18932b.
